goal: Turn GIS Development Skills from a broad documentation catalog into an installable, evidence-consistent and demonstrable GIS agent-skill product ready for a trustworthy public launch.
target: The existing GIS-Development-Skills repository on Windows; preserve the approved brand, bilingual experience, author panel, catalogs, prior skills and current uncommitted visual-asset work.
desired_outcomes: A self-contained and verifiable distribution path for the core GIS skill suite
One canonical T0-T4 evidence model with no offline/native classification drift
A runnable first golden workflow for open-source GIS development with observable artifacts and honest native-test limits
A conversion-focused README and public-site metadata that expose installation, proof and contribution paths quickly
A tested release candidate with community and publication assets prepared without performing external publication
success_criteria: A clean bundle build and isolated install-smoke test produce no missing local references
Repository checks reject inconsistent T0-T4 classifications and all current evidence labels use the canonical model
The golden workflow creates deterministic outputs with negative tests and a machine-readable acceptance report
The first README screen contains the value proposition, install path, copyable request, golden workflow and proof status with synchronized counts
All mandated catalog, skill-pack, manifest, security and unit-test commands pass, or every failure is reported with evidence
constraints: Do not overwrite or discard pre-existing uncommitted visual-asset and journal changes
Do not delete or rename existing skills, references, catalogs, templates, brand assets, author content or language controls
Preserve the exact approved English mission sentence and approved brand title/tagline
Prefer free and open tooling; disclose licensed/native GIS requirements
Do not claim ArcGIS, QGIS, browser, agent-client or packaged T2-T4 execution unless actually observed
non_goals: Guaranteeing GitHub Trending or purchasing artificial engagement
Adding more specialist domains before the distribution and evidence foundation is stable
Publishing a GitHub tag, Release, Discussions setting or repository metadata before a separate final external-action checkpoint
Certifying every external catalog entry or every proprietary GIS runtime in this revision
assumptions: The current approved implementation scope is the r1 sequence presented immediately before the user's approval
The first golden workflow should be free-first and runnable offline, with a QGIS native adapter whose native status remains NOT RUN when QGIS is unavailable

tasks.title: Build a self-contained GIS skill distribution and install smoke test
tasks.description: Add a deterministic bundle builder, package manifest and isolated verification path so the core suite retains every referenced skill, script, reference, example and template after installation.
acceptance_criteria: The bundle builder writes only to a new output directory and excludes Git metadata, development journals, caches and secrets
An isolated bundle audit reports zero missing local Markdown links and required runtime files
Documentation distinguishes source-repository installation from the verified self-contained bundle path

tasks.title: Canonicalize T0-T4 evidence and inventory truth
tasks.description: Create one machine-readable evidence-tier contract, align validators and public labels, and remove misleading current-inventory or synthetic-native classifications.
acceptance_criteria: One canonical evidence-tier registry defines T0 through T4 and is referenced by validation code
Offline fixtures are never labeled as native T2 evidence
Current README and policy inventory counts agree with the generated repository manifest

tasks.title: Create the first golden open-source GIS workflow
tasks.description: Deliver a deterministic QGIS Processing-oriented vertical slice with a pure-Python core, synthetic fixture, expected artifact, negative tests, native adapter and evidence report.
acceptance_criteria: The offline command generates and rereads a deterministic GIS artifact from a repository fixture
Negative tests cover malformed geometry, missing CRS or unsafe output behavior
The QGIS adapter and native acceptance command are documented while native status remains NOT RUN unless observed
The workflow has a copyable prompt, environment matrix and machine-readable evidence report

tasks.title: Rebuild the public front door around proof and adoption
tasks.description: Shorten the README entry experience, preserve historical detail in CHANGELOG, add proof/status surfaces, SEO metadata and contribution templates without redesigning protected brand or author content.
acceptance_criteria: A visitor can find install, copyable request, golden workflow and evidence status within the opening README section
English and Arabic counts and required mission/brand text remain synchronized
Homepage contains description, canonical and social metadata using project-subpath-safe URLs
Community files add a pull-request template and code of conduct without claiming that repository admin settings changed

tasks.title: Verify and prepare the release candidate
tasks.description: Run every mandated validator and test, audit security and skill reachability, bind DoneProof to this plan and prepare—not publish—the release notes and administrator checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog, API, skill-pack, manifest, skill-graph, security and full unit-test commands have fresh recorded outcomes
DoneProof matches every required criterion in this approved r1 plan
Release notes distinguish verified offline evidence from native and external actions that remain NOT RUN
No external release, tag or administrator-setting mutation occurs without a separate final checkpoint
